newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong says will participate in IMF's NAB.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong says will participate in IMF's NAB.

text.p: Hong Kong's de facto central bank, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority, said on Tuesday it would be one of 25 participants in the International Monetary Fund's (IMF) New Arrangements to Borrow (NAB).
The executive board of the IMF approved the NAB, a US$48 billion line of credit, to be used in situations which could threaten the stability of the world monetary system, at a meeting on Monday.
The HKMA will be participating with a share of the NAB credit line set at 340 million Special Drawing Rights (SDR), or around US$476 million.

It earlier gave the dollar figure at about US$490 million but later corrected it. "Hong Kong's participation in the NAB is of considerable significance to the territory," said Hong Kong's Financial Secretary, Donald Tsang.
"Last year, Hong Kong joined the Bank for International Settlements and we are now taking part in the NAB."
The HKMA's Chief Executive, Joseph Yam, said participation was a prudent investment in line with Hong Kong's established investment strategy.
Hong Kong's foreign reserves total around US$62.1 billion, the world's seventh largest, the HKMA said.
